narrative.overview: TravelDesk replaces the conventional left-sidebar SaaS dashboard with a top-command clearinghouse shell inspired by international aviation dispatch boards and financial clearing ledgers. A committed midnight-navy masthead anchors global role context and navigation along the top edge, freeing the full viewport below for asymmetric operational queues and persistent split-pane inspectors.
keyCharacteristics: Top 64px midnight-navy command masthead with role badge, horizontal navigation, and GSAP sliding active underline
Split-pane workbench (1.38fr / 0.96fr) keeping queues visible beside a sticky right-hand inspector dossier
Right-anchored slide-over drawers for profile, employee onboarding, policy editing, and receipt attachment
Tabular numeric alignment (Azeret Mono) across INR figures, trip IDs, and clearing timestamps

rules.name: The Two-Accent Separation Rule
rules.body: Cobalt owns orientation, selection, and progress; Signal Vermilion owns primary execution and policy flags. Never use both on the same interactive element.

rules.name: The Inline Chip Rule
rules.body: Identifiers (#19, CLAIM #9) sit inline beside headings as mono chips, never as eyebrow kickers above headings.

dos: Do keep queues visible beside docked inspectors on desktop (> 1120px) so operators retain list context.
Do apply mono (Azeret Mono) and tabular-nums to all INR currency figures, IDs, and timestamps.
Do verify contrast across both [data-theme="light"] and [data-theme="dark"] tokens.
donts: Don't place eyebrow kickers above h1/h2/h3 headings.
Don't revert to a fixed left sidebar or centered modal popups for row inspection.
Don't animate layout properties (width, height, top, left); animate transform, opacity, and stroke-dashoffset only.
